scope.description: Every production source location that owns an authoritative persistence ingress, egress, or value carried across one. Test and benchmark directories are deliberately out of scope: they may construct historical or malformed bytes, but cannot define a production storage spelling.

allowances.classification: Semantic validation/materialization of user-declared JSON bytes. The parsed value is never its durable representation; the authenticated byte tree and its explicit V1 records are authoritative.

The one explicit versioned catalogue boundary: CATS v1 length-delimits public-schema JSON, validates schema identity, and rejects any decode that does not re-encode byte-identically. This is a compatibility contract, not a private serde layout.
A malformed legacy-byte test only; the production codec never admits this postcard value.
Testing-only heap-footprint measurement behind the testing feature; bytes are discarded immediately.
Temporary in-memory comparison key for a subscription publication decision; it is never written to an OrderedKVStorage family.
In-memory normalized-query literals and a process-local policy fingerprint. The carrier is decoded before lowering and is not a persisted query or storage key.
Decodes the in-memory normalized-query literal carrier above. It is not a storage/recovery decoder.
Decodes the same in-memory normalized-query literal carrier; no durable value crosses this path.
Temporary inputs to BLAKE3 authorization scope fingerprints and their unit receipts. They are never persisted or used as a durable identity.
Testing-only footprint measurement; the result is discarded and cannot enter durable settled view state.
A test-only construction of a deliberately rejected future-format byte sequence.
Parses already-authenticated JSON bytes after a requested range is materialized; the parse result is an API value, never persisted.
